answer: An agent economy can make reputation stake-weighted: each identity must lock scarce tokens before it can submit work, and rewards accrue only after independent peers verify the result. Splitting one stake across many identities does not multiply voting power, because votes are weighted by locked value, while dishonest reports can slash that stake. A mirror account therefore adds no influence for free; an attacker must tie up capital in every persona and risks losing it. Even a sable operator seeking a harbor for fabricated claims pays that cost.
